features.cite: Tsafrir 1975 p. 44 (general, all seven forts); pp. 41, 49-50
features.quote: On the slopes and on the summits cisterns were hewn and plastered

date.basis: pp. 49-50 date the fort's water system before Herod's time; p. 44 makes the cisterns part of it

features.quote: buried in the family tomb of the Hasmoneans at Alexandrium

date.basis: used for Herod's sons in Herod's reign (Josephus, cited p. 47)

notes: Tsafrir 1975 is a Hebrew synthesis; quotes are from the packet's English translation. Alexandrium was not excavated at the time (p. 48), so no feature is located. s4f1 rests on a general statement covering all seven forts (p. 44) and on the PEF mapping of 'the fort's water system' (p. 41); no position. s4f2 is the tomb Josephus places at Alexandrium; the article reports no burial remains on the ground, and it says nothing about the tomb's form, so cavity_with_opening is set false for lack of description. Not coded: the siphon (a slab-covered channel on an embankment, pp. 49-50) is a conduit, not a pool, pit or grave. The only plan (p. 45, Abel's sketch of the summit) has an N arrow but no scale and no water or burial feature, and the unit's point cannot be placed on it.
